records.text: Austin Smith, a former Arizona lawmaker and Turning Point Action leader, pleaded guilty to attempted fraudulent schemes and illegal signing of election petitions.
records.speaker: The Associated Press

appearances.snippet: who questioned the integrity of Arizona's elections and served as a leader for the conservative group Turning Point Action is scheduled to be sentenced Tuesday for using nominating petitions that contained forged signatures in a bid to qualify for a 2024 primary election. This person is Austin Smith. He's 30. He pled guilty. In mid-November, two charges of attempted fraudulent schemes and practices and illegal signing of election petitions.

verification.notes: AP reporting and Arizona court records confirm Smith's former legislative and Turning Point Action roles and his guilty pleas to attempted fraudulent schemes and illegal petition signing.

sources.title: Former Arizona lawmaker pleads guilty in election petition forgery case
sources.relevance: Confirms Smith's roles and guilty pleas.

records.text: Austin Smith served one term in the Arizona House before abandoning his 2024 reelection campaign after petition-signature questions arose.
records.speaker: The Associated Press

appearances.snippet: Smith represented an Arizona House district in the Phoenix suburbs for one term before dropping his reelection bid in 2024 when questions arose about signatures on his nominating petition.

verification.notes: AP reporting confirms Smith served one Arizona House term and withdrew from the 2024 reelection race when questions arose about his nomination signatures.

records.text: Candace Owens said the Arizona Senate passed the Charlie Kirk memorial license-plate bill 16–2 and the Arizona House passed it 31–23.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, so this goes through, and the Senate passed the bill 16–2. Then the House of Representatives also voted in favor of the bill, 31–23.

verification.notes: Officially sourced roll-call records show the House passed SB 1439 by 31-23, but the Senate vote was 16-12, not 16-2. The extracted transcript or spoken tally dropped the digit 1 from the Senate no-vote count, so the combined statement is directly contradicted.
